newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, sets new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, sets new contract lows.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower and set new contract lows amid sentiment that U.S. wheat was still overvalued relative to world prices, traders said.
At the midsession, traders attributed the weakness in wheat to talk of competitive European prices for wheat and the EU's scrapping of a daily wheat export tax.
Wheat also saw spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans and corn, which sagged on diminished fears about frost damage.
But traders pointed out that KCBT wheat closed relatively firm, compared with other U.S. wheat markets.
"Again we saw flour-buying and very strong spot basis for hard red winter wheat," a trader said.
KCBT wheat ended 1-1/2 to 7-1/4 cents per bushel lower with Sept down 1-1/2 cents at $4.38-1/2. Dec shed 5-1/2 cents to close at $4.30, just above the new contract low of $4.28.
KCBT estimated Friday's wheat futures volume at 31.310 million bushels, versus 37.8775 million bushels Thursday.

Traders said FIMAT and Dreyfus' Term Commodities each bought nearly two million Dec bushels. Man International bought 1.5 million Dec, one million March and sold 1.3 million Dec. Refco reportedly bought and sold one million Dec.
